title: BWF Happy With World Championships Venue Overhaul in New Delhi
indian_angle: India's preparations for hosting the BWF World Championships are on track, with the BWF expressing satisfaction over the revamped Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium.
summary: The BWF has approved the overhaul of the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, ensuring its readiness to host the World Championships in New Delhi from August 17-23, addressing past operational issues.

title: Tanvi Sharma Beats Yuan An Qi to Enter Korea Masters Second Round
indian_angle: Tanvi Sharma, fresh from a Taipei Open title, secured a strong win in Korea, setting up an all-Indian clash in the next round.
summary: Fresh off her Taipei Open title, Tanvi Sharma defeated China’s Yuan An Qi in the Korea Masters opening round, advancing to face fellow Indian Shriyanshi Valishetty.

title: Kidambi Srikanth Crashes Out of Korea Masters After Losing to Daniil Dubovenko
indian_angle: Indian shuttler Kidambi Srikanth faced an early exit from the Korea Masters, highlighting a setback for a key national player.
summary: Kidambi Srikanth bowed out of the Korea Masters 2026 after losing a three-game match (22-20, 14-21, 21-12) to Israel’s Daniil Dubovenko in the men’s singles first round.

title: World Championships: Ayush Shetty to Face Defending Champion Shi Yuqi in Opener
indian_angle: Young Indian shuttler Ayush Shetty faces a challenging opening match against the defending champion at the upcoming World Championships in New Delhi.
summary: Ayush Shetty has drawn defending champion Shi Yuqi in the first round of the BWF World Championships, while PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen have relatively easier openers, and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty received a bye.

title: Satwik’s Shoulder is My Main Concern: Coach Tan Kim Her
indian_angle: Coach Tan Kim Her expressed concern over Satwiksairaj Rankireddy's shoulder, a critical issue for India's top men's doubles pair ahead of the home World Championships.
summary: Coach Tan Kim Her highlighted Satwiksairaj Rankireddy's shoulder as a primary concern, as the top Indian men's doubles pair prepares for the World Championships after a planned break for physical rehabilitation.
